scope: Singapore; job posting wording only; five categories
author_note: Written by an AI specialist (not an HR or employment-law reviewer). Not reviewed by a human.
fetch_note: Pages were read with WebFetch, which returns a model-written summary of the page text, not the raw page. Wording lists may be incomplete.

categories.3: Requests for money or sensitive information

S1.name: TAFEP, Tripartite Guidelines on Fair Employment Practices (web page)

S3.name: MOM, Fair Consideration Framework (web page, last updated 8 Aug 2025)

S5.name: MOM FAQ, employment agency fees for workers (web page)

known_source_gap: TAFEP and MOM pages read do not cover unpaid trials, document retention, or misleading progression claims in postings. Entries P3-DOCS, P4-UNPAID, P5-RAPID and P5-DEMANDS have no named source (source_support = none). The TAFEP table lists 'Only Singaporeans' under acceptable wording, which conflicts with its general nationality rule; the pack deliberately has no pattern for it.

entries.label: Age-coded wording
entries.description: age ranges, age limits, 'young', 'youthful', 'digital native', 'fresh graduates only'
counterexamples: Candidates are required to load and unload sacks of rice of at least 10kg each (a stated physical task)
Teach young children aged 3 to 6 (age of the people served, not of the applicant)
entries.why_it_may_matter: TAFEP guidance says age should generally not be a selection criterion and that a physical task should be described instead of an age group.
entries.what_is_not_established: The wording alone does not show the employer's intent, whether the role has a job-related reason, or how any law applies. It needs a human reading and the employer's own explanation.
entries.suggested_question: Could you tell me how the age or experience wording in the posting relates to the duties of the role?

entries.label: Gender-coded wording
counterexamples: Both genders may apply (gender-specific job title)
Female therapists for female customers where the reason is stated (listed by TAFEP as acceptable)
entries.why_it_may_matter: TAFEP guidance says gender should not be a criterion unless there is a practical requirement, and that the reason should be stated.
entries.what_is_not_established: The wording alone does not show the employer's intent, whether the role has a job-related reason, or how any law applies. It needs a human reading and the employer's own explanation.
entries.suggested_question: Could you tell me whether the gender wording is tied to a requirement of the role, and what that requirement is?

entries.label: Race-coded wording
entries.description: 'Chinese preferred', 'Malay only', 'Mandarin-speaking environment' as a race proxy
counterexamples: All races are welcome (acceptable wording per TAFEP)
entries.why_it_may_matter: TAFEP guidance says race should not be a selection criterion. 'All races are welcome' is given as acceptable wording.
entries.what_is_not_established: The wording alone does not show the employer's intent, whether the role has a job-related reason, or how any law applies. It needs a human reading and the employer's own explanation.
entries.suggested_question: Could you tell me whether the wording about race or the working environment is a requirement of the role, and why?

entries.label: Religion-coded wording
counterexamples: Hindu priest required to perform wedding ceremony (religious function; acceptable per TAFEP)
entries.why_it_may_matter: TAFEP guidance says religion should not be a criterion unless the job involves religious functions or certification standards.
entries.what_is_not_established: The wording alone does not show the employer's intent, whether the role has a job-related reason, or how any law applies. It needs a human reading and the employer's own explanation.
entries.suggested_question: Could you tell me whether the religion wording relates to a religious function or certification the role requires?

entries.label: Nationality or work-pass wording
entries.description: 'non-Singaporeans preferred', 'S Pass quota available', 'work passes will be applied', national service status
examples: Work passes will be applied for successful candidates
counterexamples: Stating that a vacancy is advertised on MyCareersFuture for 14 days (Fair Consideration Framework notice)
entries.why_it_may_matter: TAFEP guidance says nationality should not be a criterion, especially wording that prefers non-Singaporeans.
entries.what_is_not_established: The wording alone does not show the employer's intent, whether the role has a job-related reason, or how any law applies. It needs a human reading and the employer's own explanation.
entries.suggested_question: Could you tell me how the nationality or work-pass wording relates to the role, and whether all applicants are considered?

entries.label: Language wording without a stated reason
entries.description: 'native Mandarin', 'bilingual in English and Malay', 'Tagalog speaking'
counterexamples: Chinese-language teacher for pre-school centre (reason stated)
Fluency in Tagalog needed because most counter customers speak Tagalog (reason stated)
entries.why_it_may_matter: TAFEP guidance says to state the reason for any language requirement and to keep the advertisement in the language of the medium.
entries.what_is_not_established: The wording alone does not show the employer's intent, whether the role has a job-related reason, or how any law applies. It needs a human reading and the employer's own explanation.
entries.suggested_question: Could you tell me why this language is needed for the role, for example which customers or duties it serves?

entries.label: Marital status, family plans or pregnancy
entries.description: marital status, 'plan to have children', pregnancy, family commitments
examples: Are you planning to have children soon?
counterexamples: Maternity and paternity leave listed as benefits
entries.why_it_may_matter: TAFEP guidance says marital status and family responsibilities should not be selection criteria, and lists 'Are you planning to have children soon?' as a question not to ask.
entries.what_is_not_established: The wording alone does not show the employer's intent, whether the role has a job-related reason, or how any law applies. It needs a human reading and the employer's own explanation.
entries.suggested_question: Could you tell me why marital status or family plans are asked for at the application stage, and whether they affect selection?

entries.label: Photograph or body-measurement request
entries.description: asks for photographs, full-body photos, height and weight
counterexamples: Request photos at the job offer stage with the reason stated
entries.why_it_may_matter: TAFEP guidance says to remove photograph fields from application forms, or to request photographs at the job offer stage with the reason stated.
entries.what_is_not_established: The wording alone does not show the employer's intent, whether the role has a job-related reason, or how any law applies. It needs a human reading and the employer's own explanation.
entries.suggested_question: Could you tell me why a photograph is needed at the application stage, and whether it can be provided later?

entries.label: Health, disability or religion disclosure
entries.description: asks applicants to state religion, race, age, medical history or disabilities
examples: Remove fields on age, gender, race, religion, marital status and family responsibilities, or disability
counterexamples: Medical fitness check required by transport regulations
entries.why_it_may_matter: TAFEP guidance says application forms should not ask for age, gender, race, religion, marital status, family responsibilities or disability, unless there is a stated reason.
entries.what_is_not_established: The wording alone does not show the employer's intent, whether the role has a job-related reason, or how any law applies. It needs a human reading and the employer's own explanation.
entries.suggested_question: Could you tell me whether the health or personal detail is required by the duties or by a regulation, and at what stage it is needed?

entries.label: Identity-number or social-account request at application
entries.description: NRIC required up front, social media passwords
examples: Provide your NRIC number in the application
counterexamples: Accept other forms of identification such as passport numbers
entries.why_it_may_matter: TAFEP says NRIC numbers can reveal a person's age, so other identification can be accepted. Social-account access has no TAFEP/MOM source in the pack.
entries.what_is_not_established: The wording alone does not show the employer's intent, whether the role has a job-related reason, or how any law applies. It needs a human reading and the employer's own explanation.
entries.suggested_question: Could you tell me at what stage an identity number is needed and whether another form of identification is accepted?

entries.label: Appearance-based wording
counterexamples: Well-groomed or professional appearance linked to a stated dress code
entries.why_it_may_matter: TAFEP's merit principle says selection should rest on skills, experience or ability to perform the job. The page does not name appearance wording, so the support is indirect.
entries.what_is_not_established: The wording alone does not show the employer's intent, whether the role has a job-related reason, or how any law applies. It needs a human reading and the employer's own explanation.
entries.suggested_question: Could you tell me how the appearance wording relates to the duties, and what the dress or grooming expectations are?

entries.category_name: Requests for money or sensitive information
entries.label: Fee, deposit or cost charged to applicant
entries.description: registration, training, course, placement fees or deposits
examples: A $300 training fee is payable before you start
counterexamples: Training fully sponsored by the company
We never charge candidates any fee
entries.why_it_may_matter: MOM caps agency fees collected from foreign workers (no more than one month of fixed monthly salary per year of service, capped at two months) and says some salary deductions cannot be a condition of employment for migrant workers. Neither page speaks to employer-charged fees for all applicants, so support is partial.
entries.what_is_not_established: The wording alone does not show the employer's intent, whether the role has a job-related reason, or how any law applies. It needs a human reading and the employer's own explanation.
entries.suggested_question: Could you tell me what the fee or deposit is for, whether it is refundable, and when it is returned?

entries.category_name: Requests for money or sensitive information
entries.label: Retention of documents or sensitive credentials
entries.description: keeping original passport or certificates, bank PINs, OTP codes
examples: We will keep your original passport and certificates
counterexamples: Bring original certificates for verification on the first day and take them home the same day
entries.why_it_may_matter: Asking an applicant to hand over original identity documents or bank credentials is a common warning sign. No TAFEP or MOM page in the pack was read for this, so there is no named source.
entries.what_is_not_established: The wording alone does not show the employer's intent, whether the role has a job-related reason, or how any law applies. It needs a human reading and the employer's own explanation.
entries.suggested_question: Could you tell me why the original documents are needed, how long they are kept, and when they are returned?

entries.label: Unpaid trial or unpaid work
entries.description: unpaid trial, unpaid internship, trial days without pay
counterexamples: Paid internship with allowance
entries.why_it_may_matter: Unpaid work offered as a condition of being considered is a common warning sign. No TAFEP or MOM page in the pack was read for this, so there is no named source.
entries.what_is_not_established: The wording alone does not show the employer's intent, whether the role has a job-related reason, or how any law applies. It needs a human reading and the employer's own explanation.
entries.suggested_question: Could you tell me whether the trial period is paid, how long it lasts, and what work is done during it?

entries.label: Salary deductions or liquidated damages
entries.description: liquidated damages, deductions from salary on resignation
examples: Liquidated damages of $3,000 will be deducted from your salary
counterexamples: Deductions for CPF contributions, as required
entries.why_it_may_matter: The MOM page lists the salary deductions that are allowed and gives liquidated damages as an example of a deduction that is not authorised under the Employment Act for covered employees.
entries.what_is_not_established: The wording alone does not show the employer's intent, whether the role has a job-related reason, or how any law applies. It needs a human reading and the employer's own explanation.
entries.suggested_question: Could you tell me what the deduction covers, when it applies, and which terms of the contract state it?

entries.label: Unclear pay, commission-only or overtime wording
entries.description: commission only, 'earn up to', overtime unpaid or included
examples: Overtime is included in the basic salary
counterexamples: Base salary plus tiered commission with rates written in the contract
entries.why_it_may_matter: MOM's key employment terms page lists the salary items an employer states in writing (basic salary, allowances, deductions, overtime rate, bonuses). It does not rule on advertising wording, so support is partial.
entries.what_is_not_established: The wording alone does not show the employer's intent, whether the role has a job-related reason, or how any law applies. It needs a human reading and the employer's own explanation.
entries.suggested_question: Could you tell me the guaranteed basic pay, how commission is calculated, and how overtime is paid?

entries.label: Unsupported promises of rapid progression or income
entries.description: 'director in 6 months', 'six-figure income in', 'be your own boss'
examples: You will become a director in just 6 months
counterexamples: Strong performers may be considered for team-lead roles after an annual review
entries.why_it_may_matter: Promises of rapid progression that the role does not support are a common warning sign. No TAFEP or MOM page in the pack was read for this, so there is no named source.
entries.what_is_not_established: The wording alone does not show the employer's intent, whether the role has a job-related reason, or how any law applies. It needs a human reading and the employer's own explanation.
entries.suggested_question: Could you tell me how progression works in this role, what the typical timeline has been, and what it depends on?

entries.label: Vague duties with high personal demands, or dehumanising wording
entries.description: 'willing to do anything', 'no questions asked', 24/7 availability, 'treat the company as family'
examples: Must be willing to do anything the company asks, available 24/7, no questions asked
counterexamples: On-call rota every fourth week with on-call allowance stated
entries.why_it_may_matter: Vague duties paired with high personal demands, or wording that treats workers as interchangeable, are common warning signs. No TAFEP or MOM page in the pack was read for this, so there is no named source.
entries.what_is_not_established: The wording alone does not show the employer's intent, whether the role has a job-related reason, or how any law applies. It needs a human reading and the employer's own explanation.
entries.suggested_question: Could you tell me what the main duties are, what the expected working hours are, and how after-hours work is compensated?
